text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended with pared losses as the market recovered from early afternoon lows. The London market started on a firm tone but this proved to be short-lived as Indonesian producer hedge selling re-emerged and scale-down roaster buying fizzled out. The September contract eventually closed $13 down at $1,785 per tonne.

Arabica futures in New York ended mixed in light dealings with commission house selling pressuring the nearby contracts, traders said. September ended at 165.70 cents/lb, down 2.65 cents/lb on the day and just short of the session high of 166.50 cents/lb. Spot July ended down 2.25 cents/lb at 185.25 cents/lb, while the outer months closed up 0.35 to 2.25 cents/lb.

ICO - The International Coffee Organisation (ICO) said producing members' exports reached 81.75 million 60-kg bags in the 12 months to May 1997, up sharply from 73.02 million in the same 1996 period. In May, exports rose slightly to 7.03 million bags from 7.02 million in April.

This compares with 6.60 million in May 1996. In the first eight months of the current 1996/97 (October/September) coffee year to May, total exports were up at 57.36 million from 50.11 million the same 1995/96 period.

The ICO export data confirm once again that producers undertook large shipments in order to take advantage of high prices. Some in the trade thought the figures were bearish as the 9 million bag increase in exports in the 12 months through May 1997 reflected a less dire stock situation than many market participants had feared.
UNITED STATES - US certified coffee stocks as of July 4 rose by 1,926 bags to 52,476 60-kg bags. There were 35,930 bags pending grading.

PERU - Peru's May coffee production increased 9.5 per cent to 558,550 bags, from 510,283 bags in May 1996, the Agriculture Ministry said. This brought cumulative production in the first five months of 1997 up to 945,050 bags, down from 965,383 bags in the same period the previous year.

Non-decaffeinated coffee exports in the first five months were worth $24.6 million, down from $32.6 million in the same period last year. Peru, whose principal coffee harvest is between April and November, is South America's number four producer after Brazil, Colombia and Ecuador, according to the government.

GUATEMALA - Guatemala exported 257,000 60-kg bags of coffee in June, bringing the total exports to a record of just under 4 million bags for the 1996/97 harvest. The country's exports have now well exceeded Anacafe's original estimates for the total crop.

Some coffee remains in the country for export, though Anacafe does not know the quantity. Anacafe originally estimated that Guatemala would export 3.7 million bags in the 1996/97 harvest (October/March). The exports for June 1997 were down sharply from the same period last year, when the country shipped 337,000 bags.

NEW ZEALAND - Coffee imports in May 1997 amounted to 10,900 60-kg bags, down from 13,501 bags imported in May 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first five months of 1997 up to 64,289 bags compared to 66,485 bags in January/May 1997. Major suppliers of green coffee in 1997 were Vietnam (17,700 vs 14,000 bags) and Papua New Guinea (11,300 vs 9,300 bags).
